Isn't this all expected, since we're trying to extract as many referenced issues as possible from the main issue? Ideally, we should match all these cases except for the third one, as long as we can fit the content within the context. No, re-ranking and embedding search, is different. Re-Ranking, uses the query (the question) and documents (the similar issues and comments), and ranks them in order of relevance to the query, this uses something `Cross Encoder`. This is very similar to embedding, but does not require us to create/manage embeddings.
And, yes in theory the documents, could be text strings from any source.
tldr; we extract similar issues/comments (Our DB) and then rank them in order for a relevance search(voyage reranker) with the question asked.
The Claude SDK has never worked for me with Openrouter. The only benefit it offers is the ability to cache system messages for 5 minutes.
I can manage these cases on a case-by-case basis; the alternative would be more complex. I assume, similar to "Resolves #1234," there are only a few cases like this?

[Without the structured representation](https://github.com/sshivaditya2019/test-public/issues/181#181)

2. Fix Links in Responses [Issue](https://github.com/ShivTestOrg/test-public/issues/247#issuecomment-2590998114)

Earlier, we retrieved all the contexts and tried to include everything in the context. In this approach, it's the opposite: we first extract the root issue or pull request review comment, then find similar issues and comments. Starting with the body of each issue and comment, we look for any references to other issues or pull requests. This process is repeated recursively until we reach either the maximum depth or token limit.
Once we have all the relevant data, we restructure it into a tree format (which could potentially be converted to XML). The final structure will always be smaller than the original recursive retrieval, as unnecessary tokens will be removed. This ensures there is always enough space for the output tokens.
TL;DR: This method enables us to fetch data at depths of up to 30 (or more), as long as it fits within the context memory.

- there should not be two comments for the failure
- the context should be truncated in some way to allow `/ask` to run properly
## What was expected
`/ask` should truncate the context so it runs properly and still gives an accurate answer.
## How to reproduce
